incidents.vector: Compromise of one of the platform's six liquidity vaults, exploiting flaws in protocol-owned funds handling.
incidents.impact: Roughly $10.7 million in Bitcoin and other tokens stolen; trading halted and signing activity automatically suspended. The Swiss-based cross-chain platform says user funds were not affected.

incidents.vector: Active exploitation of CVE-2026-20182, a CVSS 10.0 authentication bypass in Cisco Catalyst SD-WAN Controller and Manager that lets unauthenticated attackers impersonate a hub router and gain administrative access.
incidents.impact: Threat cluster UAT-8616 — overlapping with Chinese Operational Relay Box networks — used the flaw to add SSH keys, modify NETCONF configurations, and escalate to root on victim controllers. Cisco patched the bug and CISA added it to the KEV catalog with an emergency directive for federal agencies.

incidents.victim: OpenAI, Mistral AI, UiPath (TanStack supply chain)
incidents.vector: TeamPCP group seeded credential-stealing malware (Shai-Hulud worm variant) into 84+ npm packages, including the widely-used TanStack React framework, which self-propagated to almost 400 downstream packages.
incidents.impact: OpenAI is rotating macOS code-signing certificates after two employee devices were compromised and limited credential material was exfiltrated from internal repositories; macOS users must update by June 12. Mistral confirmed source code repos were temporarily breached and the attackers are offering Mistral source code for sale. Worm source code was subsequently leaked publicly, raising risk of follow-on attacks.

incidents.vector: Ransomware intrusion by the Nitrogen group (using custom tooling derived from Conti and ALPHV code) against North American factories; data theft followed by encryption.
incidents.impact: Several Foxconn factories in North America were disrupted; the company says affected sites are resuming production. Nitrogen claims to have stolen 8 TB / 11 million files, allegedly including confidential project files tied to Intel, Apple, Google, Dell, and Nvidia. Foxconn has not confirmed any ransom demand.

incidents.victim: European government and diplomatic targets (incl. Ukraine)
incidents.vector: Russian FSB-linked actor 'Secret Blizzard' (Turla) deploying the modular Kazuar malware family, which has evolved into a peer-to-peer botnet with Kernel, Bridge, and Worker modules that elects a single 'leader' to handle external C2 over HTTP, WebSockets, and Exchange Web Services.
incidents.impact: Long-running covert espionage access into government and diplomatic networks across Europe and Central Asia, and into systems in Ukraine previously compromised by Russian GRU-linked Aqua Blizzard — supporting Russian foreign-policy and military intelligence collection.

incidents.victim: Ukrainian and Polish government and military organizations
incidents.vector: Spearphishing campaign by Belarus-linked group FrostyNeighbor (also tracked as Ghostwriter / UNC1151) using PDF lures impersonating Ukrainian telecom Ukrtelecom, with server-side IP-based victim validation that delivers a JavaScript PicassoLoader downloader and Cobalt Strike payload only to selected Ukrainian targets.
incidents.impact: Continued espionage and credential-collection operations against Eastern European government and military targets in support of Belarussian and Russian interests; victims that don't match operator-chosen criteria receive only a benign decoy.

incidents.victim: Instructure / Canvas LMS (≈9,000 schools and universities)
incidents.vector: ShinyHunters (tied to the Scattered Spider / Lapsus$ collective) initially accessed Instructure via voice-phishing of staff and an issue tied to Free-for-Teacher accounts; on May 7 the group re-compromised the same path and defaced the Canvas login page with a ransom demand.
incidents.impact: Canvas was taken offline mid-final-exam season, disrupting coursework at thousands of K-12 districts and universities; ShinyHunters claimed 3 TB of data including names, emails, student IDs and private messages on up to 275M users. Instructure paid the ransom and obtained 'shred logs' confirming destruction; House and Senate committees have demanded briefings from CEO Steve Daly.

incidents.vector: A 23-year-old train enthusiast used commodity software-defined radio hardware to spoof a 'general alarm' message on THSR's TETRA emergency radio system, which appears to have been deployed without proper authentication or key management.
incidents.impact: Three high-speed trains were ordered to perform emergency braking and were halted for roughly 48 minutes, triggering an anti-terrorism response and renewed scrutiny of cyber-physical risk in legacy rail communications worldwide.
